items.titulo: ESPN's first Super Bowl will play live in IMAX theaters
items.resumen: Hundreds of IMAX screens in the US and abroad, Australia and Brazil included, carry the game on February 14, 2027. Will the commercial breaks reach theaters?

items.titulo: Wall Street Journal tells all bots to keep out, except more than 60
items.resumen: Search crawlers and three OpenAI scrapers made the guest list, and Barron's and MarketWatch share the rule. Can a file bots may ignore get AI firms to pay?

items.titulo: Off-topic videos can draw 10 views or 10 million, YouTube tells creators
items.resumen: No channel-wide score exists in YouTube's algorithm, so a creator's million-view average promises nothing off-topic. Can a variety channel still hold together?

items.titulo: Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads drops to $4.99 a month for a year
items.resumen: Premium falls to $14.99 from $21.99 for new and returning US sign-ups through November 30. What do cheaper sign-ups to the ad plan mean for Disney ad sales?

items.titulo: YouTube's free phone editor now stacks video, text and sound in layers
items.resumen: Captions, overlay clips and several audio tracks each get a row that creators can mute or hide. YouTube has not said how many tracks fit, or in which markets.

items.titulo: Prime Video renews Rings of Power for season 4 with no date or cast
items.resumen: Filming starts this spring at the UK's Shepperton Studios, no year given. Season 3 took about 17 months from cameras to screen. Will Prime members wait as long?

items.titulo: No sale, no pay: Taboola links 60 brands with 21,000 creators
items.resumen: Howl, the creator network Taboola bought in August, claims over $1.5bn in gross sales. Brands pay only per sale, so sales tracking sets what each brand pays.

items.titulo: Amazon's CTO says the 20-watt brain will shape the next computers
items.resumen: IT chiefs now ask Werner Vogels about geopolitics before cost, and his 2027 list has company AI agents attacking code before launch. What changes for ad data?

items.titulo: YouTube quietly tests a mute button in its Android app
items.resumen: Spotted on Android app version 21.46.522, the speaker icon sits beside full screen for some users only. Would an ad silenced with it still count as a view?

items.titulo: Pixalate estimates fake TVs cost advertisers $135 million in six months
items.resumen: Fake TV identities that reset every midnight posed as 3,277 streaming apps, from Hulu to Tubi. Why did 77% arrive through sellers the apps never authorised?

items.titulo: Discord's December 15 policy names ad IDs it collects on sponsored content
items.resumen: Impressions, clicks and conversions from ad partners enter Discord's privacy policy for anyone who engages with Quests. How much can new settings switch off?

items.titulo: In B2B, the safe brand beats the better product, LinkedIn argues
items.resumen: Being able to defend the choice topped five buyer motives at 34% among 750 senior B2B buyers. What about the finance and procurement staff that ads never reach?

items.titulo: Etsy plans to enforce its unedited-photo rule from early 2027
items.resumen: Cropping, resizing and watermarks are now allowed on the required photo if no AI tool touches it. Refunds apply already; which listings are exempt from it?

items.titulo: Character.ai still faces Kentucky's chatbot lawsuit during bankruptcy
items.resumen: Louisville firm FBT Gibbons, owed $11,180.90, is named as local counsel in Kentucky's case. Objections close December 15, a week after the sale hearing ends.

items.titulo: Character.ai moves to keep the law firm it owes $146,382 on three lawsuits
items.resumen: Munger, Tolles & Olson lists past or current work for Google, OpenAI and Disney. Objections to its role in the three chatbot lawsuits are due by December 15.

items.titulo: KPMG could earn up to $5.1m finding Character.ai a California tax refund
items.resumen: Fees fall from 30% of the first $2m to 10% above $18m, paid only once California pays. The filing's own timeline runs to 10.5 years if the state pushes back.

items.titulo: The typical Google Ads sale costs European shops 14% more, Channable finds
items.resumen: Median cost per sale went from €14.41 to €16.47 for over 10,000 EU online shops while click prices held flat. Will Black Friday weekend push the rise past 20%?

items.titulo: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy exits after more than 11 years
items.resumen: Product and technology chief Balaji Thiagarajan and the board now run a marketplace of 1.4 million sellers. A successor is due in weeks; no listing date is set.

items.titulo: MonetizeMore says 10.8% of the traffic it checked was bots posing as people
items.resumen: Easy-to-catch bots were 0.4%. For ad buyers and publishers, its CEO says AWS's new auction filters see only the request. What can a check before the bid miss?

items.titulo: Amazon blocks 20 of 24 AI agents by name, the most of 79 top US retailers
items.resumen: Invitations to named AI agents at 79 big US chains rose from 1 in 2024 to 63 in 2026, with Ulta Beauty at 11. Does a written welcome actually let the bots in?

items.titulo: Fast fashion, slow parcels: SHEIN to pay the FTC $100m
items.resumen: Five phone agents for nearly 1m US parcels a day, the FTC alleges. The order sets delay notices and review rules for SHEIN. When will buyers see their refunds?

items.titulo: OpenAI adds over 2,000 internet addresses ChatGPT uses to visit websites
items.resumen: Sites that verify ChatGPT visits by address now meet 130 new blocks, taking the list from 237 to 367 entries. What the capacity is for, OpenAI has not said.

items.titulo: Best-of lists climb to 65% of AI Black Friday toy links, iPullRank finds
items.resumen: Brand websites got no lift in AI answers as Black Friday 2025 neared, and ChatGPT runs about two weeks ahead this year. Data for 2026 lands after Cyber Monday.

items.titulo: Trade Desk says direct connection lifted DAZN Media+ auction revenue 41%"
items.resumen: Bids sent direct to Kayo Sports, BINGE and Foxtel won 2.9 times as often as bids routed via middlemen. How much of the gain was new money is not disclosed.

items.titulo: Daily Search Forum Recap: November 25, 2026
items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today...

items.titulo: Spain fines Axesor €160,000 for reselling self-employed workers' data
items.resumen: Tax-office records on self-employed people reached buyers through 364 Axesor contracts in five years. Deletion is ordered. What changes for B2B lead lists?

items.titulo: Google Ads Encourages Dynamically Scoring Conversion Values Hack
items.resumen: Ginny Marvin, the Google Ads Liaison, said that the Google Ads platform "we strongly encourage" "dynamically scoring conversion values" and they do not consider it a "hack" of any kind. "Optimizing for deep conversion actions and feeding high-fidelity, first-party data is the best way to steer the system to what you value most," she added.

items.titulo: Google AdSense Opt-Out, Messaging & Privacy Updates
items.resumen: Google AdSense posted a few updates related to regulatory changes around opt-out controls, messaging and privacy regulations for the ad product. I figured I'd group them into one post and sum it up.

items.titulo: What Does ‘Performance’ Actually Mean for TV? Buyers Weigh In
items.resumen: What does performance actually mean in TV environments? And what do media buyers need to achieve that performance? These two questions were the focus of a panel of buyers at this year’s Go Addressable event in New York City on Thursday. The post What Does ‘Performance’ Actually Mean for TV? Buyers Weigh In appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Meta's Muse AI can now shop at Walmart, but Walmart picks the products
items.resumen: Shoppers set a spending cap in a Walmart Agent Profile and pay in the chat with a saved card. Walmart says more apps and agents will follow on the same route.

items.titulo: Amazon Can’t Quit ChatGPT; Manipulative Mobile Game Ads Win
items.resumen: Happy Thanksgiving! The AdExchanger team will be taking the rest of the week off to enjoy the holiday. The Daily News Roundup will return on Monday, Nov. 30. Never Attribute To Malice Name two bigger frenemies in ecommerce than OpenAI and Amazon. The two companies are headed for a showdown over online shopping, argues Mike […] The post Amazon Can’t Quit ChatGPT; Manipulative Mobile Game Ads Win appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Game: The cheapest impressions are usually the ones nobody watched
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups for Thursday. One set comes from this week's coverage, and a few tiles would fit just as well at a summer ballpark.

items.titulo: Catalan regulator folds AI privacy and rights checks into one 64-page form
items.resumen: Lenders, insurers and public bodies that deploy high-risk AI can owe both reviews from December 2027. What the form asks, and where its own scoring math slips.

items.titulo: Finance apps now pay for 1.83 installs for every free one, Adjust finds
items.resumen: Lending apps now see 3.92 paid installs per free one and India 6.5, while next-day returns slip to 11.5%. Which finance apps keep the users their ads bring in?

items.titulo: AI agent makers that skip user controls face action, UK's ICO warns
items.resumen: Guidance for consumer AI agent builders is due in spring 2027, after a call for evidence that closed November 20. What will count as a meaningful user control?

items.titulo: UK privacy watchdog keeps its Meta correspondence on Muse AI secret
items.resumen: Seven questions on Muse, children and autism drew no documents from the UK regulator. Its draft thinking on AI companions stays private until that work ends.

items.titulo: Ondato's selfie age check wins certification for New York's kids law
items.resumen: Social platforms in New York may misjudge 17-year-olds as adults at most 15% of the time from January 25. No public list yet shows which age checks qualify.

items.titulo: Ads drive 68% of US short drama app downloads, Sensor Tower finds
items.resumen: Monthly users of apps such as ReelShort rose 93% in 2026, but churn neared 60% and third-quarter in-app sales fell 28%. What happens when ad budgets slow down?

items.titulo: UK app makers get four months to collect from Google's £260m settlement
items.resumen: Each UK developer that paid Google Play commission from August 2018 can claim at least £200. Claims close March 24, 2027, then the tribunal reviews payouts.

items.titulo: Disney's $20m Character.ai deal faces objection from US bankruptcy watchdog
items.resumen: Releases Disney won before the bankruptcy can't be approved now, the US Trustee says, adding that Google's $2.7bn is unexplained. A judge weighs it December 7.

items.titulo: Character.ai drops request to hide who backs its $10m bidder
items.resumen: Octave Fund I LLC backs the bid for users' chats, AI models and ad data. Creditors now ask why the only executive files searched belong to an ex-CEO at Disney.

items.titulo: Character.ai's creditors pick a $1,500-an-hour adviser to check the sale
items.resumen: Contractors could bill up to $2,500 an hour, and two of the three committee members are minors. A hearing is set for December 15, a week after the sale hearing.

items.titulo: Character.ai loses $3.3m in its first 20 days in bankruptcy
items.resumen: Cash still rose to $63.9m because most October bills were not yet paid, and staff fell to 8. What the report tells creditors before the December 7 sale hearing.

items.titulo: TikTok bans devices after Maldita finds child abuse posts with 48m views
items.resumen: Only 5 of 50 abuse videos Maldita reported were removed, and Spain sought a suspension. TikTok's reply now points advertisers to three brand safety filters.

items.titulo: Google preannounces a December core update as AI Overview links slide down
items.resumen: Google preannounced a December core update and explained how AI answers pick links, as data showed links sliding in AI Overviews and Amazon bought ChatGPT ads.

items.titulo: Google On How Links Are Selected & Shown In AI Overviews & AI Mode
items.resumen: As part of the updated documentation and Google Search ranking hub we covered a new document named Attribution and factuality in Search generative AI features. This document is chock-full of information on how Google selects which links to show in AI Mode, AI Overviews and other Search generative AI features.

items.titulo: Google publishes its search ranking principles 23 days before a UK deadline
items.resumen: AI Overviews, maps and web links face one usefulness test, Google tells site owners. A December update is next. What can publishers check, and what is missing?

items.titulo: Google On Inventory Pages Per Geographic Region: Fewer Pages Better
items.resumen: Google's John Mueller gave advice on how to handle inventory pages for each geographic area that you might have. Instead of creating a page for each product and geographic area with its inventory, create a single product page and show the inventory levels for that product in each location, without creating a new page for each location.

items.titulo: Bing Image Search Ask Visual Search Button
items.resumen: Microsoft seems to be testing a new button when you overlay your mouse cursor over an image in the Bing Search results. Previously, a visual search button took you to a new screen when clicked; now, an Ask button lets you add context to your query for that image search.

items.titulo: Google Image Collections & Saved Items Adds Ask Anything AI Mode
items.resumen: The Google Images collections & saved items section added an "Ask anything" button, where it will take all the images in the collection and let you ask Google AI Mode about them in one shot. Yes, Google is even sticking AI Mode into the images you save to your collections in Google Image Search.

items.titulo: Google Snoopy Thanksgiving Prep 2026 Doodle
items.resumen: Tomorrow is Thanksgiving in the United States and Google is getting ready with a new Thanksgiving 2026 prep Doodle or logo. You can see the characters from Snoopy preparing the Thanksgiving table outside in this animated Doodle.

items.titulo: 31% of US homes with LG TVs plan bigger holiday budgets, 65% in Brazil
items.resumen: For TV advertisers: viewing on UK LG sets beat normal levels on all 39 days of last season, Brazil's on just 13. What can a survey of 2,000 LG owners tell them?
